reviews.comment: Content of course isn't difficult, but the strict grading can quickly take your grade down. Lectures were usually just spent deriving formulas, which made things more complicated than necessary. She does do exam reviews and tells you the content to expect and gives some bonus pts. Exams and quizzes were very fair but be careful with math errors.

Knowledgeable, but she speeds through heavy math and can convolude simple topics. She deducts an undeservedly high number of points for minor algebraic mistakes or notation errors on quizzes and exams. Bonus points on HWs and exams compensate for this well. Content-wise, an easy class, and grade-wise too, if you are careful.

Tropina knows what she's talking about, but isn't great at transferring that to students. She speeds through derivations without fully explaining them, but gives opportunities for students' questions. She redeems herself by telling you exactly what will be on the exams and how to do the homework.

Easily the worst instructor ever. She was rude and demeaning to students. She would bundle multiple true/false questions into a single grade, so one tiny mistake meant losing all the points. Quizzes had no partial. On exams she would pick and choose which workout question had partial. He justification was always "engineers don't make any mistakes."

Attendance is not mandatory, but lecture notes are not published. Quizzes are graded with no partial credit. When attending office hours, be cautious with the information provided, as it has occasionally been inaccurate; referencing the textbook is often more reliable.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Understanding her words is the biggest challenge you will face in the course. I do not know what kind of English she speaks, but I do know English would have been better off without her speaking it. Next comes enduring her classes. Will open her slides and write the equations in a white paper. Just that and nothing else. Never provides solutions.
Great professor. Her lectures were genuinely interesting, and they were very helpful for the exams. It is very clear what you are expected to know going into exams.

Lectures are not engaging or very useful. It was mostly a bunch of derivations that we hardly use. I used the lecture slides only on all the quizzes and homeworks. I think I could have skipped the lectures entirely. The course is straightforward if you can decipher these lecture slides.
Tropina is amazing. She cares about you succeeding and her test reviews pretty much go through the test questions before hand. She is super brilliant and loves to teach. I highly recommend her
Pay attention during class and practice problems before tests.

Tropina is one of the best professors I've had. She genuinely cares about her students and wants you to be successful and learn. She explains the material really well and is willing to elaborate/clarify if something is not clear. Her tests are fair and not meant to catch you of guard. Nothing she does is meant to trick you. Take her if you can!

she says exactly what's gonna be on exams+lots of extra credit so those are easy A's. but her bi-weekly quizzes are graded harshly (frqs but u either get all points or none) so those can bite. bi weekly hws arent graded harsh. hw & quizzes alternate. not the best lectures but textbook's great & she tells u what to read & well organized canvas page

Dr Tropina is a great prof. Her lectures can get a little scattered at times but the course is overall very organized and it's clear what you need to learn for each exam. In fact in class she goes over what specific types of problems you will see. She also adds extra credit to many homeworks/exams

If you go to class and pay attention, the class is super easy. Tropina is very nice and makes everything very simple and direct. The homework is manageable, and she basically tells you exactly what is on the exams so it's easy to do well on them. Bonus points are offered on almost every assignment. Overall, a great prof

Only critique is she will call on students and make them participate even if they do not want to. Other than that, super nice gives easy tests and she creates all of her lecture notes by hand in class which makes notetaking easy. Willingly participate in class and she will tend to favor you. Probably the best-dressed professor in the department.

For Aero 301, I think Dr. Tropina is the best professor out there. She very clearly tells you exactly what problems are on the quizzes and exams and will work them out in class before the exam. The exam is almost exactly like these problems. Show up to lecture, period. In addition she provides an enormous amount of extra credit.

Tropina definitely enjoys 301 more than 222. There may be a bit of a cultural barrier most of the time but I think Tropina really cares about the students and the class. She goes over each type of problem that will be on the exams and its a lifesaver. Homework and quizzes rotate every week. Make sure to ask for a joke at the end of each class!

Tropina is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet, but she hates teaching AERO222. HW's are long and grueling, very coding heavy (I'm a comp sci minor and they were still really hard) and Tropina doesn't teach much coding just super heavy math theory. Only bright side is exams were relatively easy compared to HWs. A's are possible but difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you don't have programming experience before taking this class, get some experience. Lectures are hard to understand but lots of time to submit homework and tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not terrible. TAs are a lifesaver. Coding helps understanding of content. Randomly calls on you in class- be prepared. Teamwork helps for learning. Doesn't grade harshly, just do the work. Ask for a joke at the end of class :) GO TO LABS. If you are ever lost the textbook will help but its the equivalent to googling.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The coding homework assignments were god awful and took up to 15 hours to complete. Her lectures don't make any kind of sense and are impossible to follow. Also, she cant do arithmetic. When trying to do Gaussian elimination she gives up halfway through because she makes so many arithmetic errors that it becomes hopeless. Shes a sweetie tho

Terrible, terrible, terrible, terrible. Couldn't teach to save herself. Each lecture, without fail, leaves the class more confused about the subject than before. The curriculum is non-existent. Very nice human being though.

Thick accent, purposefully writes trick questions on her quizzes where you only have five minutes. Her lectures are impossible to follow mainly because she has a heavy accent, and constantly switches between power point and handwritten notes

There were many aspects of Dr. Tropina's teaching style that should improve with experience but at the moment most of the lectures leave much to be desired. Slides with good content were given to students outside of class, but, she often did not use them during lectures. We had a good lab TA which made a huge difference.

Dr. Tropinas method of teaching can best be described as sporadic. The structure of the class is strikingly different than that of the mirrored 220 class. Not to mention that things are changing throughout the semester (and Im only halfway done with the course). I understand it may be her first year teaching, but it aint off to a good start.
